find-refs (formerly US-045): rt inspect find-refs --json emits a JSON array of { symbol, kind, file, line, column, snippet } objects; one entry per reference site; sorted by (file, line).
find-refs: RtCommandInfo.JsonOutput = true; help text describes the schema; --help shows the JSON shape under an 'Output' section.
find-callers (formerly US-046): rt inspect find-callers --json emits a JSON array of { caller, file, line, column, callerSignature } objects.
find-callers: RtCommandInfo.JsonOutput = true; integration test covers a method with two callers in two files.
find-undocumented (formerly US-047): rt inspect find-undocumented --json emits a JSON array of { symbol, kind, file, line, accessibility } objects; one entry per public/internal API lacking xml doc.
find-undocumented: respects existing --include-internal flag; integration test covers a class with mixed documented/undocumented members.
find-unused (formerly US-048): rt inspect find-unused --json emits a JSON array of { symbol, kind, file, line, accessibility, reason } objects.
find-unused: reason is one of 'no-references' | 'only-self-references' | 'only-test-references'; matches the existing plain-text categories.

circular-deps (formerly US-049): rt analyze circular-deps --json emits a JSON array of cycle objects, each with { cycleId, projects: [...] } where projects is an ordered list forming the cycle (last project depends on first).
circular-deps: when no cycles exist, emits an empty array '[]' to stdout (not '{}' or null); exit code 0.
find-magic-strings (formerly US-050): rt analyze find-magic-strings --json emits a JSON array of { literal, occurrenceCount, sites: [{ file, line, column, contextSnippet }] } objects.
find-magic-strings: respects existing --min-occurrences flag; sorted by occurrenceCount descending.
list-imports (formerly US-051): rt analyze list-imports --json emits a JSON array of { file, imports: [{ namespace, alias, isStatic, isGlobal }] } objects; one entry per source file.
list-imports: --top N (if it exists today) flag still works in JSON mode.
list-smells (formerly US-052): rt analyze list-smells --json emits a JSON array of { smell, severity, file, line, message, suggestion } objects sorted by severity descending then file.
list-smells: severity is one of 'low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'critical'; matches the plain-text output classification.
All eight commands honour the existing --json global flag plumbing (no per-command --json reinvention); RtContext.Format == OutputFormat.Json triggers the JSON branch.

All eight commands route diagnostics/progress to stderr; only the JSON document goes to stdout in JSON mode; stdout JSON parses cleanly via System.Text.Json.JsonDocument.Parse with zero leading/trailing non-JSON text.
rt dump-help output reflects JsonOutput=true for all eight commands after the change; docs/COMMANDS.md regenerates locally with updated metadata.

Architecture test enforces the JSON-shape contract: a per-command snapshot test runs each command against a fixture solution and asserts the JSON output matches an approved snapshot (e.g. tests/RoslynTools.Tests/Cli/JsonOutputSnapshotTests.cs).
dotnet build clean; dotnet format --verify-no-changes clean; existing tests pass; new snapshot tests added under tests/RoslynTools.Tests/Cli/.
Smoke: each of the eight commands invoked against RoslynTools.slnx with --json exits 0 and produces parseable JSON in under 60 seconds.
Stories can be parallelised inside this umbrella: each command is independently shippable as a sub-batch under EP-007. /execute may pick any subset of the eight ACs to land per run.
